# `m.crypto.daily_open_close`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

The open and close prices of crypto pairs on one UTC day, with the trades behind them.

```python
m.crypto.daily_open_close(symbols, date)
```

[All datasets](README.md)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Verbs | `fetch()`, `poll()` |
| Served by | REST |
| `poll()` | `dm.PollMode.REPLACE`: holds exactly the latest cycle's rows, keyed by `Symbol` |

## Arguments

What each argument does for this dataset, and the rule it follows for every dataset that takes it.

| Argument | For this dataset | For every dataset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `symbols` | Crypto pairs, such as `X:BTCUSD`. `dm.ALL` is refused; use `m.crypto.bars(dm.ALL, dm.Timespan.DAY).history(day, day)` instead. | Massive's ticker for each symbol, spelled exactly as Massive spells it: `AAPL` or `BRK.B` for a stock, `O:SPY271217C00700000` (the OCC code) for an option, `I:SPX` for an index, `C:EURUSD` for a forex pair, `X:BTCUSD` for a crypto pair, and `ESZ6` for a future. Pass one symbol as text, several as a list, or a table with a `Symbol` column. A live table is followed: each symbol you add is read, and each one you delete stops being read. `last_by()`, `fetch()`, `history()`, and most polls also drop a deleted symbol's rows. `dm.ALL` reads every symbol, and leaving the argument out reads every record with no filter by symbol, where this dataset takes them. A misspelled symbol in text or a list raises `ValueError` at the call; by default, a misspelled row of a table is skipped and logged, and the table keeps running. `dm.canonical_symbol` converts other spellings to Massive's. A record that lists several symbols, such as a news article, appears once for each symbol you named that it lists. |
| `date` | The UTC day, as a date such as `"2026-01-02"`. A `datetime` or an instant is refused. | One calendar day, as text such as `"2025-06-02"`, a Python `date`, or a Deephaven `LocalDate`. It means the day in the market's time zone: New York for stocks, options, and indices; UTC for forex and crypto; for futures, the trading session that ends that day. A `datetime` or an instant is refused at the call. |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The instrument, in the library's canonical symbol form. From REST `symbol`: "The symbol pair that was evaluated from the request." | REST |
| `Date` | String | The day the summary covers, as ISO yyyy-MM-dd text: a UTC calendar day. From REST `day`: "The date requested." | REST |
| `TimestampStart` | Instant | The start of the day the summary covers, as an Instant: 00:00 UTC of `Date`. A summary whose `IsUtc` is false covers its date's day in a zone Massive does not name, so its window is the widest that day has in any zone: from 14 hours before 00:00 UTC of `Date` to 12 hours after 00:00 UTC of the next day, with a WARNING. | REST |
| `TimestampEnd` | Instant | The exclusive end of the day the summary covers, as an Instant: 00:00 UTC of the next day. A summary whose `IsUtc` is false covers its date's day in a zone Massive does not name, so its window is the widest that day has in any zone: from 14 hours before 00:00 UTC of `Date` to 12 hours after 00:00 UTC of the next day, with a WARNING. A row read before its window ended has `TimestampInsert` before `TimestampEnd`, and its values can still change; `t.where("TimestampEnd <= TimestampInsert")` keeps only the rows read after their window ended. That test reads the local clock, which can be off, and a row read within moments of its end, or from a delayed feed, may still lack the window's last trades; an end set later than the window's (an index day's extra hour, a stamp kept as sent) only keeps a finished row out longer. | REST |
| `RawSymbol` | String | The symbol exactly as Massive sent it, on a row whose spelling the library cannot read as the dataset's class (its `Symbol` is then null); null on every other row. Present unless the session's `unreadable_symbols` is `dm.OnError.RAISE`, which fails on such a row instead. | REST |
| `Open` | double | The open price for the symbol in the given time period. | REST |
| `Close` | double | The close price for the symbol in the given time period. | REST |
| `ClosingTrades` | String | An array of results containing the requested data. The column holds Massive's value as JSON text. | REST |
| `IsUtc` | boolean | Whether or not the timestamps are in UTC timezone. | REST |
| `OpenTrades` | String | An array of results containing the requested data. The column holds Massive's value as JSON text. | REST |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST |
